title: auth-api-401-429-debug-scratchpad-ethan-2026-03-30
content:
Goal: capture breadcrumbs for recurring 401/429s reported by customers on /v1/generate and /v1/chat endpoints. Hypotheses: 1) API key TTL/rotation propagation issue; 2) per-key quota enforcement bug (race on update); 3) IP-based burst detection + global quota; 4) client retry semantics causing bursts causing 429.

Quick repro commands tried:
- curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"prompt":"hello","max_tokens":10}'
  -> 401 {"error":"Unauthorized","code":401}
- curl -I https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $GOOD_KEY' (works)
- Replayed request with same key from different IP (via ngrok) -> sometimes 429 with headers: Retry-After: 10, X-RateLimit-Limit: 120, X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
- Checked auth service logs (filtered by key_id): saw token validation success then quota check failing (quota lookup returned null) -> downstream service returned 429

Observed patterns:
- 401s mostly when key was just-created via admin UI (~<60s). Possible propagation delay in caches (redis cluster?)
- 429s occur in bursts correlated with client-side fanout (10-20 concurrent short requests) from same api_key
- Some 401s come with TLS renegotiation around same time (rare) — raised for infra/SRE to check load balancer
- Not all keys affected; subset belong to same org/tenant

Commands / probes run:
- hit /internal/key-status?key_id=... -> returned "active" but cache TTL showed last-write timestamp mismatch
- curl -v to auth endpoint to inspect headers: saw X-Auth-Cache-Hit: 0 for failing keys
- ran redis-cli --latency on auth cluster (narrow spikes ~3-4s observed during windows)

Immediate mitigations to try:
- increase cache TTL on auth read-miss fallback to reduce window (temp)
- add jitter/backoff client-side and recommend to customers (client library update)
- enable request-level logging for affected key_ids for 24h (privacy aware)

Next steps / TODOs:
- [ ] Ask identity team (Aisha) to dump cache invalidation logs around 2026-03-27 23:00-01:00 UTC for tenant X
- [ ] Run controlled load test with key rotation enabled to reproduce propagation delay
- [ ] Instrument quota service to log null lookups + source (redis vs db) (owner: Samir)
- [ ] Confirm LB TLS renegotiation metrics with SRE
- [ ] Draft customer-facing status blurb once root cause confirmed

Notes / breadcrumbs:
- Related slack: #infra-auth thread (link in linked_artifacts)
- Customer report: "errors started after rotating keys via UI"
- Workaround for customers: create new key, wait 2m before using, or use existing key

If hitting 401: check Authorization header format (extra spaces/newline) and clock skew (rare). If hitting 429: check client concurrency, X-RateLimit headers and advise exponential backoff. Keep live notes here as we iterate.
